recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. No FHIR source follow-up is needed for FHIR-11141 unless the Security WG wants a new, separate change to the current Provenance delegation semantics or target profile list.
issue_request: FHIR-11141 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for the Security WG. It asked Provenance.agent to support the organization or organizational part that a user acted on behalf of by adding a Signature.onBehalfOf-like structure, and also contemplated replacing the older Provenance.agent.actor/userId shape with a Signature.who-like agent identity structure.
initial_application: Commit d6bec27176add2738ac0b05bd3dddcc177ab67ff explicitly included GF#11141 and changed the old Provenance spreadsheet/examples by adding Provenance.agent.who[x] and Provenance.agent.onBehalfOf[x], while marking Provenance.agent.actor, Provenance.agent.userId, and the old relatedAgent structure as deleted.
additional_context: Provenance is active in source/fhir.ini. The current StructureDefinition has Provenance.agent.who as the acting agent Reference and Provenance.agent.onBehalfOf as the optional delegating-authority Reference. Later Provenance cleanup, including the already-published FHIR-14370 commit on the combined branch, removed stale userId-era wording rather than restoring old actor/userId elements. Direct Zulip and Confluence searches for FHIR-11141 found no conflicting community record.
reconciliation: No source change was needed. The current source preserves the issue's substantive model by pairing the acting agent with a same-agent onBehalfOf relationship, and signatures guidance explicitly aligns Signature.who/onBehalfOf with Provenance.agent.who/onBehalfOf.

related_jiras.note: Removed stale Provenance userId wording after the old actor/userId model had been replaced; already represented on the combined branch and used only as context here.

Later Provenance Reference-definition work moved STU3 who/onBehalfOf choices away from URI-style values toward Identifier/Reference representation, explaining why the current syntax differs from the 2016 resolution text.
